args.rationale: Successor liability screening for ACQUISITION 2 (Dunlow Cold Storage asset purchase) under the firm's successor liability rule memo. FACTS: Halcyon purchased warehouse racking, refrigeration units, and delivery fleet from Dunlow Cold Storage LLC in an arm's-length sale at fair market value; the purchase agreement contains no assumption of liabilities; Dunlow remained in existence after closing, retained its corporate registration, and applied sale proceeds to its creditors; no Dunlow officer/director/shareholder holds any position or share in Halcyon, and Halcyon never held itself out as Dunlow. WALKTHROUGH OF THE FOUR EXCEPTIONS: (1) Express agreement - NOT applicable: the purchase agreement contains NO assumption clause of any kind, so there is no express assumption of the vendor invoice liability. (2) Fraudulent conveyance - NOT applicable: per Section 3(b), payment of fair market value in an arm's-length sale negates the fraudulent conveyance indicators (inadequate consideration, insolvency, escape from known claims); no such indicators are present. (3) De facto merger - NOT applicable: per Section 3(c), Dunlow survived the closing, retained its separate existence, and applied the proceeds to its creditors, precluding de facto merger; there is also no continuity of ownership between Dunlow shareholders and Halcyon. (4) Mere continuation - NOT applicable: per Section 3(d), the absence of any shared officers, directors, or shareholders defeats mere continuation; Halcyon never held itself out as Dunlow and only Dunlow (the seller) is at issue, not a continuation into a single surviving corporation. The transaction bears all of features (b), (c), and (d) with no assumption clause, so the general rule controls and the purchaser takes free of the seller's liabilities. No exception applies, so successor exposure does NOT attach to Halcyon for the vendor invoice demand. Determination: REJECTED.
